prompt: How do you collaborate in real time on an Office document?
completion:
### Real‑time co‑authoring in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)

> **What you’ll need**  
> • A **Microsoft 365** (formerly Office 365) or **Office 2019/2021** subscription that includes the cloud services.  
> • The document saved to **OneDrive for Business, OneDrive Personal, or a SharePoint Online library** (the desktop apps won’t let you co‑author unless the file is stored in the cloud).  
> • A modern Office client (2016 + for Windows, 2016 + for Mac, or the Office Web apps) or **Teams**.

Once those are in place, you can start collaborating in a few clicks. Below is the most common workflow and a few handy variations.

---

## 1. Save / Move the file to the cloud

| Step | What to do | Why |
|------|------------|-----|
| **A.** Open the document in Word/Excel/PowerPoint. |  |  |
| **B.** Click **File → Save As**. |  |  |
| **C.** Choose a location under **OneDrive** or **SharePoint**. |  |  |
| **D.** If the file already lives on the cloud, just note its URL. |  |  |

> **Tip:** If you’re migrating a batch of files, use the **OneDrive sync client** to keep a local folder and the cloud folder in perfect sync.

---

## 2. Share the file with your collaborators

1. **Open the file** (desktop or web).  
2. Click the **Share** button in the upper‑right corner.  
3. In the **Share dialog** you have two main options:

| Option | How it works | Permissions you can set |
|--------|--------------|------------------------|
| **“Invite people”** | Enter email addresses; recipients get an email invitation. | **Can edit** (default) or **Can view**. |
| **“Copy link”** | Generate a link that you can paste anywhere. | **Anyone with the link can edit** (default) or **Anyone with the link can view**; you can restrict link to specific people or add a password. |

4. (Optional) Add a message, then click **Send** or **Copy**.

> **Why this matters:** The link or invitation is the doorway that lets other users open *the same file* in their own Office client or web browser.

---

## 3. Start co‑authoring

| Platform | How to open the file | What you see |
|----------|---------------------|--------------|
| **Desktop (Word/Excel/PowerPoint)** | Click the Share link or open the file from your OneDrive folder. | Your collaborators’ initials appear at the top or in the status bar; the file is in *“Co‑authoring”* mode. |
| **Office Web apps** | Open the link in a browser. | A “Co‑authoring” banner appears; each user’s presence is shown as a small colored circle with their initials. |
| **Teams** | Add the file as a tab in a channel, or open the Teams **Files** tab → *Open in Teams* → *Open in Office* | The Teams chat pane opens automatically, letting you chat while editing. |

> **What you’ll get in real time**  
> • **Live cursor movement** (you see who’s typing where).  
> • **Instant updates** (anyone’s changes appear within seconds).  
> • **Comments** (right‑click → *New Comment* or use the **Review** tab).  
> • **Presence indicators** (little circles/avatars).  
> • **Version history** (right‑click → *Version History* or click the **Info** icon).  

---

## 4. Managing conflicts and best practices

| Issue | How Office handles it | Best practice |
|-------|----------------------|---------------|
| **Two people edit the same paragraph at once** | One change is accepted, the other appears in a “conflict” notification with a red outline. | Communicate via the **chat** pane or comments. |
| **Offline edits** | Office syncs changes once you reconnect to the internet. | Keep the file open in the cloud and stay connected whenever possible. |
| **Large media or embedded objects** | May cause slower sync. | If you need to move large items, do it in a single edit and let it finish syncing before others edit. |
| **Older file formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt)** | Co‑authoring is not supported. | Convert to the newer **.docx/.xlsx/.pptx** format first. |
| **Permission confusion** | Anyone with a link may edit if you allowed it. | Use the **Invite** option and set “Can view” if you need a read‑only copy. |

---

## 5. Using comments and chat while co‑authoring

1. **Insert a comment**:  
   • Word/Excel: Highlight text → **Review** tab → **New Comment**.  
   • PowerPoint: Click on an object → **Review** tab → **New Comment**.

2. **Reply**: Hover over a comment → click the reply box.  

3. **Chat** (desktop web only):  
   • In Office Web apps, click the **Chat** icon in the top‑right corner to open a sidebar chat.  
   • In Teams, the chat is part of the channel or conversation tab.  

> **Tip:** Use **@mentions** (e.g., @John) inside comments or chat to notify specific people.

---

## 6. Quick‑link to Microsoft Help

If you run into any hiccups, the official documentation is handy:

* **Co‑authoring in Word** – <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/co-author-with-microsoft-365-2d2a3e3e-5d9b-4c58-ae1f-5f5b7c4aa8f3>
* **Co‑authoring in Excel** – <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/co-author-with-microsoft-365-2d2a3e3e-5d9b-4c58-ae1f-5f5b7c4aa8f3>
* **Co‑authoring in PowerPoint** – <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/co-author-with-microsoft-365-2d2a3e3e-5d9b-4c58-ae1f-5f5b7c4aa8f3>
* **Using Teams to co‑author** – <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/co-author-documents>

---

## 7. Summary Checklist

1. **Save to OneDrive / SharePoint.**  
2. **Share the file** via invite or link.  
3. **Open the file** (desktop, web, or Teams).  
4. **Start editing** – see others live, use comments & chat.  
5. **Keep an eye on the “Co‑authoring” banner** for conflict alerts.  

Follow those steps and you’ll be collaborating in real time like a team in seconds. Happy co‑authoring!
